title: Leaky formats stay out of mastery gates
statement: Keep item formats that leak as a family out of every mastery gate, serving them, if at all, only in a practice lane that never gates progress.
example: One reading plan records choice-family argument items leaking about 98.6% by construction.
detail: A Grade 8 reading course built to a full-coverage target gate-assesses all 15 plan standards from a certified-only item pool, with its leaky formats confined to a non-gating practice lane. Its case for review counts 5 gating formats and a 43-item lane in three formats for format exposure, never routed through a mastery gate, with 0 audit errors, and says zero leaky and zero broken items serve among its gating items; its coverage matrix tells any agent to keep the partition. A Grade 7 plan drops all-choice assessment, recording that choice-family argument items leak about 98.6% by construction.
against: A record already there asks that every item a check fails leave what learners see, not only scoring, and the review behind it allowed only confinement to non-gating slots, which this lane is. In the same bank, multiple-choice and two-part evidence items rebuilt to need the passage are gating formats, so whether a format leaks as a family depends on how its items are built.

evidence.quote: full item-type coverage, with the leaky formats confined to a non-gating practice lane.
5 gating formats (text_entry, sequence, mcq, ebsr, inline_choice) + a **43-item non-gating practice lane** (multi_select, hot_text, match) for
format exposure, never routed through a mastery gate (all `gating:false`, 0 audit errors).
Served is a strict subset of certified; **zero leaky and zero broken items serve.**
Preserve the gating/practice partition; leaky formats never route through a mastery gate.
